title: Remapping Ctrl (Left) to Caps Lock remaps Middle Mouse Button action

status.label: Tracked in #18979
status.detail: The same Ctrl-to-Caps Lock and touchpad-gesture symptom is already tracked in open #18979; maintainers closed #23383 as a duplicate of that issue. This is a tracking disposition, not a claim that the bug is fixed.

next_action: Keep the touchpad gesture and unexpected-key-event investigation on open issue #18979; avoid a competing fix for this duplicate report.

judgment.rationale: This report describes remapping Left Ctrl to Caps Lock and having a touchpad middle-click gesture produce the Windows Project panel and toggle Caps Lock. Open issue #18979, "TouchPad gestures cause unexpected key events," reports the same Ctrl/Caps remapping and three-/four-finger gestures producing Win+P and Caps Lock. Maintainers closed #23383 as a duplicate of #18979 and closed #36711 as a duplicate of #23383; #36711's report is nearly identical to this issue. #18979 remains open, so this is a duplicate tracking route, not a claim that a fix shipped.
evidence: Issue #26982 is open, unassigned, and has one public comment; its 2026-10-11 activity is only a product-label update.
The report says PowerToys 0.70.1, remaps Left Ctrl to Caps Lock, and observes a middle-click touchpad action opening Win+P and toggling Caps Lock.
Open issue #18979 describes Left Ctrl/Caps Lock remapping with touchpad gestures producing Win+P and Caps Lock; later reports also describe unexpected Ctrl events from gestures.
A maintainer closed #23383 as a duplicate of #18979, explicitly stating it is the same Keyboard Manager/touchpad gesture bug.
Issue #36711 reports Ctrl-to-Caps Lock with touchpad three-finger tap producing Win+P and Caps Lock; a maintainer closed it as a duplicate of #23383.

A 2022 maintainer comment on #18979 explains that Windows sends the gesture as a key event which Keyboard Manager sees through its low-level keyboard hook, and that the hook cannot identify it as a touchpad gesture.
At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:414-420 looks up remaps by the low-level event vkCode; it does not identify the input's originating gesture.
judgment.recommended_action: Track the unresolved touchpad-gesture behavior on #18979; do not propose a separate fix for this duplicate.

fix_assessment.rationale: No competing fix is proposed for this duplicate. The broader gesture-generated-key behavior remains open and tracked in #18979; this disposition does not imply the defect is fixed.

issue_context.summary: The reported Ctrl-to-Caps Lock plus touchpad middle-click behavior matches the broader touchpad-gesture-generated-key issue still tracked in #18979.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.70.1 and says Left Ctrl is remapped to Caps Lock.
A middle-click touchpad gesture is reported to open Win+P and toggle Caps Lock.
Open issue #18979 covers touchpad gestures causing unexpected key events while Ctrl/Caps Lock remapping is active.
Maintainers closed #23383 as a duplicate of #18979 and #36711 as a duplicate of #23383.
The current #26982 issue has no assignee; the latest activity only changed its product label.
inferences: The touchpad driver or Windows gesture layer appears to generate a keyboard event that Keyboard Manager then remaps, but this issue's original report does not establish the exact event sequence.
The duplicate relationship is strong enough to avoid a separate fix proposal, while the open canonical issue means the broader behavior is not marked resolved.
issue_context.analysis: The linked reports provide a stronger tracking path than this older duplicate. The canonical issue remains open and includes later reports of similar unexpected key events, so preserve the unresolved status there rather than closing this issue or claiming an existing fix.
